mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה holds 'raising the partition', which תנא wrote the משנה about immersing for חולין versus מעשר, and רב מרי's lesson about חולין kept at the purity of קודש
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא brought as a challenge to רבי יוחנן. In it, רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר about immersing in the upper of two stacked pools, which shows that רבי יהודה does not hold the idea of 'raising the partition'. רבי יוחנן accepts this: if the ברייתא says so, it says so. The גמרא then goes back to our משנה, which says that immersing for חולין does not count for מעשר, and explains that this is the view of the רבנן, who treat חולין and מעשר differently. But the end of the same משנה lists levels of purity with no separate level for מעשר, which sounds like רבי מאיר. The גמרא's first answer is that the משנה is split: the beginning is the רבנן and the end is רבי מאיר. רב אחא בר אדא avoids the split by reading five levels at the end, so the whole משנה follows the רבנן. Finally, רב מרי learns from the משנה that חולין prepared with the purity standards of קודש are treated like קודש, and the גמרא asks where this comes from. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה reporting that רבי מאיר allowed immersing in the upper pool, while he himself allows only the lower one. This shows that רבי יהודה does not hold 'raising the partition'.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יהודה said:] רבי מאיר used to say: one may immerse in the upper pool. But I say: in the lower one, and not in the upper one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it brought to challenge רבי יוחנן. In it, רבי יהודה openly disagrees with רבי מאיר about immersing in the upper of two stacked pools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had said that רבי יהודה holds the idea of 'raising the partition' (גוד אסיק). That idea is what would let the upper pool join up with the lower one and count as a full מקוה. Since רבי יהודה here forbids immersing in the upper pool, it looks like he does not hold that idea, and that is the challenge to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Immerses (a person or a vessel) in a מקוה
The upper (pool)
The lower (pool)
'Stretch it up': picturing a wall as rising higher than it really does

phrases.english: [Rabbi] Meir would say: One may immerse in the upper one,
and I say: In the lower one,
but not in the upper one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאִיר הָיָה אוֹמֵר: מַטְבִּיל בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה, וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: בַּתַּחְתּוֹנָה וְלֹא בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the earlier lines brought against רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהודה holds 'raising the partition'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה held 'raising the partition', he would allow immersing in the upper pool. He forbids it, so he must not hold that idea.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that if this ברייתא is really taught, then he accepts it. So רבי יהודה does not hold 'raising the partition'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן does not try to answer the challenge. He simply agrees that if the ברייתא says this, it must be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a concession, not a defense. רבי יוחנן accepts that his earlier claim about רבי יהודה cannot stand against a clear ברייתא. The result is that the question of 'raising the partition' is a real argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it is taught, it is taught': I accept the ברייתא and can't argue with it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן gives in: the ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה does not hold 'raising the partition'.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
phrases.notes: Based on the earlier lines, the one answering here is רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 1 by accepting it
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge stands. רבי יהודה does not hold 'raising the partition', and רבי יוחנן accepts this.

steps.title: Whose view is our משנה about immersing for חולין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the line in our משנה about immersing for חולין and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who immersed for חולין and took on the status of purity for חולין' and so on. Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's line about immersing for חולין and asks who the author is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if someone immersed only for the sake of חולין, the immersion does not count for מעשר. The גמרא wants to know which תנא's opinion matches that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: One who immerses himself
Ordinary food that is not holy
He took on the status (here, a status of purity)
Whose view is our משנה?

phrases.english: One who immersed for non-sacred food and assumed the status for non-sacred food, etc.
phrases.notes: 'כו׳' means 'and so on'. The משנה goes on to say that he is forbidden to eat מעשר.

phrases.english: Whose is the mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא goes back to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא wrote the rule that immersing for חולין does not count for מעשר

steps.title: The answer: it is the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows the רבנן, who treat חולין and מעשר differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the רבנן, who make a difference between חולין and מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this part of the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only someone who treats מעשר as stricter than חולין would say that immersing for חולין is not enough for מעשר. The רבנן hold that view, so this line must be theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Who make a difference (between the two)
Tithe produce (here, מעשר שני), which is holier than חולין

phrases.english: It is the Rabbis,
who differentiate between non-sacred food and tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן הִיא, דְּשָׁנֵי לְהוּ בֵּין חוּלִּין לְמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן, because they treat חולין and מעשר as different levels

steps.title: Look at the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה: an עם הארץ's clothes count as מדרס for פרושים, and פרושים's clothes count as מדרס for those who eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the end part: The clothes of an עם הארץ are מדרס for פרושים. The clothes of פרושים are מדרס for those who eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It quotes the end of the same משנה, which lists levels of purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list jumps straight from פרושים (people who keep חולין pure) to those who eat תרומה. It has no separate level for people who eat מעשר. That suggests whoever wrote this part treats מעשר just like חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the end part': look at the later section of the same משנה
Someone who is not careful about the laws of purity
Impurity from a זב sitting or treading on something; it makes the item a main source of impurity
People careful to eat even חולין in purity

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean these clothes were actually stepped on by a זב. It means that, for someone at a higher level of purity, they are treated as if they had been.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
The garments of an am ha'aretz are treading-impurity for perushin.
The garments of perushin are treading-impurity for those who eat teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a challenge to the answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה has no separate level for מעשר. That fits someone who treats חולין and מעשר the same, not the רבנן.

steps.title: Does the משנה switch authors halfway?
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה matches רבי מאיר, who treats חולין and מעשר the same. Can the first part be the רבנן and the end be רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: So we have come to רבי מאיר, who says חולין and מעשר are the same! Is the first part the רבנן and the end part רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge plainly. The end of the משנה follows רבי מאיר, and it is strange for one משנה to change authors midway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 gave the first part to the רבנן. The list in step 5 fits only רבי מאיר. Normally we expect one משנה to follow one opinion all the way through, so splitting it between two authors sounds forced.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We have come to': this now matches the view of...
They are like each other, the same
The first part... and the end part (of a משנה)

phrases.english: We have arrived at Rabbi Meir, who said:
Non-sacred food and tithes are similar to one another.
The first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying the משנה follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the end is רבי מאיר and the beginning is the רבנן, the משנה would have two authors, which is unusual.

steps.title: Yes, the משנה is split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the split: the first part is the רבנן and the end part is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes: the first part is the רבנן and the end part is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by agreeing to it. This משנה really does follow two different authors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of finding a way to read the whole משנה as one opinion, the גמרא accepts that it was put together from two views. It is unusual, but this answer accepts it. The next step gives a different answer that avoids the split.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is split. Its first part (immersing for חולין doesn't count for מעשר) is the רבנן. Its end part (the list of מדרס levels with no separate level for מעשר) is רבי מאיר.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אִין' looks like a short throwaway word, but here it is the whole answer. The גמרא is agreeing to the split it just called strange.

phrases.english: Yes, the first clause is the Rabbis
and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, רֵישָׁא רַבָּנַן וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by accepting the split
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge: the משנה is split between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single משנה should follow one author all the way through
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is the רבנן and the end part is רבי מאיר

steps.title: רב אחא בר אדא reads five levels so the whole משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אדא has a different version of the end of the משנה, with five levels instead of four. That keeps the whole משנה in line with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אדא would teach the end of the משנה with five levels, and in this way he explains the whole משנה according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the problem from steps 6–7. Instead of splitting the משנה between the רבנן and רבי מאיר, רב אחא בר אדא learns the end of the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version we had, the end of the משנה jumps straight from פרושים (people who eat חולין in purity) to those who eat תרומה, skipping מעשר. That looked like רבי מאיר, who puts חולין and מעשר on one level. רב אחא בר אדא's version adds a separate level for מעשר, making five levels. Now חולין and מעשר are separate, just as the רבנן hold, so the whole משנה follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the משנה
Levels or steps of purity, each one stricter than the one before
He sets it up, meaning he explains it as following a certain opinion
All of it, the whole משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to handle the משנה. Either the start follows the רבנן and the end follows רבי מאיר (step 7), or, like רב אחא בר אדא, we read five levels at the end and the whole משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא בר אדא does not disagree about what the רבנן or רבי מאיר hold. He disagrees only about the wording of the משנה: his version has an extra level, so it no longer matches רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא מַתְנֵי לַהּ
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Adda would teach it
with five levels in the end part,
phrases.notes: The version we had shows four levels here. His version adds a separate step for מעשר, between חולין and תרומה.

phrases.english: and he explains all of it according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּסֵיפָא חָמֵשׁ מַעֲלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer instead of the split accepted in step 7: change the wording of the end of the משנה so no split is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different version of the text (five levels instead of four)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the משנה puts חולין and מעשר on one level, like רבי מאיר, so the משנה has to be split between two תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: With five levels, the end of the משנה separates חולין from מעשר, and the whole משנה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: רב מרי: חולין kept at the purity of קודש count like קודש
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי learns from the משנה that חולין prepared על טהרת הקודש are treated like קודש. The גמרא then asks where in the משנה this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: We can learn from the משנה that חולין prepared with the purity standards of קודש are like קודש. From where do we see this?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section opens. רב מרי draws a halachic lesson from our משנה, and the גמרא's question 'מִמַּאי' sets up the proof, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally חולין have the lowest purity standard. רב מרי says that if someone chose to handle his חולין with the stricter purity rules of קודש, they are treated at the level of קודש. He does not yet show where the משנה teaches this. The גמרא's question opens the way for that explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: a lesson drawn out of a source
Non-sacred food prepared with the purity standards of sacred food
They are like, they are treated as
From what? Where do you see this?

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the level of purity a person chooses to keep can decide how his food is treated, even when the food itself is only חולין.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: Learn from it
phrases.notes: 'It' is our משנה about the levels of purity.

phrases.english: non-sacred food that was prepared with the purity of sacred food
is like sacred food. From where do we see this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the question of which תנא the משנה follows to a new halachic lesson drawn from the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין prepared על טהרת הקודש are treated like קודש.
